top.title: DL Gabriel Truss survived severe car accident to earn second chance at college football
top.description: Garden City Community College defensive lineman Gabriel Truss committed to Eastern Michigan this weekend. The Eagles have a good class of JUCO additions coming in, but Truss is a little different. He is a 6-foot-3, 320-pound run stuffer who has college experience having played at Missouri Western State prior to coming to Garden City. What makes him extra unique are the circumstances that brought him to Garden City and have made him so appreciative of every day he gets to play football and simply be alive. “I got in a car accident and thought I’d never play football again,” Truss said. “I had split my jaw almost in half, I was missing my bottom four teeth, I fractured the top of my spine, broke my leg, fractured rib, I had a concussion, and had emergency jaw surgery.” The early days in the hospital were tough. “There were days when I was in terrible pain,” Truss said. “I’d be in my hospital bed, pressing my button and waiting for the nurse to come bring me pills to take away the pain and I tried not to question why God put me through this. But my faith played a big factor. I’m so thankful now for getting offers to play at the next level.” Eastern Michigan proved to be that right opportunity, with his official visit to Ypsilanti sealing the deal for Truss. “I would say the coaches, their hospitality, and their interest in me made me want to be there. And I liked the facilities, the meeting rooms and all that,” Truss said. With that, Truss now prepares for the next step of his journey, which is enrolling mid-year at Eastern Michigan. “Getting this opportunity, coming from where I’m from and being through what I’ve been through, I just am very thankful,” Truss said. Truss had 16 tackles (2.5 for loss) this season for Garden City.

top.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo Ruled Out for Heat’s Showdown Against Thunder
top.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images The Miami Heat will be missing a crucial piece of their lineup as they prepare to face the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday. Star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo has been ruled out due to a groin injury, marking his first missed game since joining the Heat in the offseason. Antetokounmpo, a former two-time MVP, has been instrumental in Miami’s early success this season, averaging an impressive 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60.2% from the field across 15 games. His absence will undoubtedly be felt as the Heat look to maintain their momentum. The Thunder, too, will be without star power, as reigning two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is sidelined with a lower back contusion and neck strain. Both players were initially listed as questionable, but the decision to keep them out comes as both teams navigate through the challenges of the season. Miami is speculated to look to Bobby Portis Jr. to step into the starting lineup in place of Antetokounmpo. Portis brings energy and experience, but replacing the production and leadership of Giannis will be a tall order for the Heat. As the Heat entered Sunday with a record of 9-6, sitting in sixth place in the Eastern Conference, the team is keen to capitalize on their home court advantage. The Thunder, meanwhile, are dealing with a slew of injuries to key players, including Alex Caruso, Jaylin Williams, and Chet Holmgren, which has tested their depth. While both Antetokounmpo and Gilgeous-Alexander are playing at an All-NBA level this season, the Heat will need to rally together in Giannis’s absence. With the stakes high, Miami aims to secure a victory and keep pace in the competitive East. Fans will be eagerly watching to see how the Heat adapt and who steps up in this pivotal matchup.

top.description: FEATURE | Five things we learned from Bundesliga Matchday 10 The Bundesliga returned following the final international break of the year, and what a spectacle it was. From a swing of the title race pendulum, to changes at the bottom of the table, Get German Football News has you covered with the latest talking points after Matchday 10. Here are five things we learned… Bayern Munich have an attacking problem This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse. Even with Kane fit, Bayern have been wasteful in front of goal this season. Granted, some of the results the ball just wouldn’t go in, like against Schalke and Augsburg, but the difference between this season and last year was that Bayern would prove to be far more clinical in front of goal, but Germany’s record champions seemed to have lost that edge now, as shown in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday night. This has resulted in games where Bayern should win comfortably being a lot more difficult, mainly due to their own doing. With the injury to Kane, and with no fit back-up, this problem is likely to get worse and could make or break Bayern’s Bundesliga season. It’s now up to Vincent Kompany and his coaching team to find a solution, and quick. top.title: Studs and duds from Bears' 21-13 win against the Saints
top.description: The Chicago Bears have now won five straight games after taking down the New Orleans Saints, 21-13, in Week 11. They still had two turnovers in this game, although they also forced two takeaways and scored 13 points off of them. Jeffery Simmons had one of the best games of his career, while Montez Sweat also had the Bears ’ first safety in nearly five years. Offensively, things stalled after the second quarter. Still, quarterback Caleb Williams finished the game with two touchdowns and completed over 65 percent of his passes. Chicago also got Salvon Ahmed involved in the running game and he finished with 33 rushing yards on just six carries. Here are mostly studs and a few duds from the Bears’ win against the Saints, including All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who tied his career-high in sacks in this game with three, and cornerback Jaylon Johnson, who once again struggled in coverage. Stud: DT Jeffery Simmons What a game for Jeffery Simmons. Throughout his career, he has always played well when facing New Orleans, but this was one of the best games of his entire career. Simmons tied his career-high in sacks with three. His only other game with three sacks was back in 2021. He now has five sacks in three games since joining the Bears. This trade has immediately paid off for Chicago and turned them into a championship-caliber defense. Dud: CB Jaylon Johnson After having a pick-six in Chicago’s last game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Jaylon Johnson returned to his regular-season form in this game. It felt like every time there was a blown coverage in this game, mostly against Chris Olave, Johnson was the one in coverage. The Bears’ weakness on defense is certainly their secondary and Johnson is a major reason why, since he is severely underperforming. Stud: WR Zavion Thomas This may have been the NFL’s introduction to Chicago’s rookie wide receiver, Zavion Thomas. His speed was on full display with his 30-yard run to set up the Bears’ second touchdown of the game and his impressive 40-yard catch on third-and-17 to set up Chicago’s field goal in the third quarter. However, his diving catch on a broken third-down play in the fourth quarter may have been his best play of the day, even though the Bears did not end up scoring on that drive. New Orleans’ secondary slowed down most of Chicago’s playmakers, but they could not stop Zavion Thomas. Dud: RB D’Andre Swift New Orleans clearly emphasized stopping the Bears from running the ball. top.title: ‘Worse outcome’ – Mike Pettine’s defense was worse than Christian Parker’s, says former Dallas Cowboys star
top.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Tennessee Titans to move to 5-6… But what about their defense? Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys’ offense stole the show against the Titans, winning 51-30. Ahead of the game, all the talk was about the team’s defense, after they promoted Mike Pettine to call plays in place of defensive coordinator Christian Parker. The switch was a response to the 46-40 loss to the 49ers, in which the Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards. Speaking after the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was pleased with the way the defense played. He told his press conference: “Overall, I was very proud of the defensive unit, coaches, and everybody.” But his response did not please former Cowboys wide receiver Isaiah Stanback, who told the Cowboys’ postgame show that he felt the defense actually went backwards. He pointed to the fact the team gave up 30 points against a Titans team that is now 1-9 in the standings. Isaiah Stanback: Cowboys went backwards “I don’t wholly agree with him,” Stanback said, in response to Schottenheimer being proud of the Cowboys’ defense. He explained: “Last [week], he faced one of the more prominent offenses in the [offensive] play caller, and some of the most dangerous weapons in the NFL. He faced one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL, Brock Purdy. “Christian McCaffrey, one of the best running backs you have played in the game, as far as catching the ball, running the ball. “You got five sacks against [a] San Francisco 49ers outfit. You got five sacks against the Tennessee outfit that has Cam Ward, has Tony Pollard, Chimere Dike, that’s a big difference, right? “You gave up 46 last week. You gave up 30 to a Tennessee Titans team, that came in averaging 18 points per game. “So you can feel as if you performed better, but in reality, if I’m looking at it in totality, yes, you gave up more yards. Yes, you gave up bigger plays. All that stuff last week, but it was against a substantially better outfit. “So, to me, as I look at this, I think giving up 30 to this outfit is actually a worse outcome than even what you faced last [week], in my opinion.” The Cowboys’ defense will be tested next against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, who secured a surprise 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. top.title: Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera charged with DWI in Montgomery County
top.description: Héctor Herrera on the pitch during a Houston Dynamo match in July. (Maria Lysaker/Getty Images) Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated Saturday in Montgomery County, according to the sheriff's office. Herrera, 36, whom the team signed to a one-year deal in January, has bonded out of the Montgomery County Jail, according to Miranda Hahs, director of public affairs for the sheriff's office. Herrera's name did not appear in county court records or the jail inmate roster Sunday afternoon. Hahs did not answer further questions about the player's bail. No further information about the incident was available. The arrest comes days before the Dynamo are scheduled to begin the playoffs Tuesday in San Jose, Calif. The Tijuana, Mexico native was the Dynamo's highest paid player in 2022 with a salary of over $5 million. He's making $525,000 this year, according to the Football Reference online database. In a statement to the Chronicle, team communications manager Jack Holmes said the club and Major League Soccer are aware of Herrera's arrest. "The Houston Dynamo are aware of an incident involving Héctor Herrera on Friday night. The Club and Major League Soccer are working to gather additional information.We will refrain from providing further comment until appropriate," the statement read. top.title: It’s a Deal! Skubal to the Mets!
top.description: Sep 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images It’s Official! Tarik Skubal is a New York Met . The New York Mets have agreed to terms with two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal on a nine-year, $450 million contract , according to multiple reports on Sunday. The deal, first reported by the New York Post’s Jon Heyman and confirmed in its terms by ESPN’s Jeff Passan, sets a new standard as the richest contract ever given to a pitcher in MLB history. The agreement includes a $45 million signing bonus, full no-trade protection, and no opt-out clauses. Roughly $30 million is deferred. The average annual value comes to $50 million, also a record for a pitcher and well clear of the previous high-water marks set by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. It eclipses Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s 12-year, $325 million pact with the Dodgers by $125 million in total value. Skubal, who turned 30 last week, becomes the centerpiece of a Mets rotation that already features promising right-hander Nolan McLean. He joins a lineup built around Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette. For owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns, the signing is the clearest statement yet that the club intends to rebound from a disappointing 2026 season and contend immediately in 2027. The left-hander’s path to free agency was eventful. After winning consecutive Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025 with the Detroit Tigers, he underwent a procedure in May 2026 to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. He returned in roughly six weeks and was later traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers ahead of the deadline. Across both clubs in 2026, he went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings. Because he changed teams midseason, the Dodgers could not make him a qualifying offer, so the Mets incur no draft-pick penalty for the signing. Skubal’s free-agent process moved quickly. He held in-person meetings last week in California with the Mets, Dodgers, Blue Jays, and Padres. New York was widely viewed as the favorite after an early offer in the neighborhood of nine years and nearly $400 million. Agent Scott Boras had indicated a strong likelihood the left-hander would decide before the collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1. Over the past three seasons, Skubal has posted a 2.42 ERA, ranking among the game’s elite in strikeouts, innings, and Wins Above Replacement. He has also shown postseason pedigree, with a career 2.13 ERA in eight playoff starts. The Mets are betting that version of Skubal remains the one who takes the mound in Queens for the rest of the decade.

top.title: Eagles vs. Steelers: The good, the bad, and the ugly
top.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Joe Milton III #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It looks like Nick Sirianni has his job for another week. It looks like the Eagles are heading towards a threepeat as NFC East champions, and another playoff run in 2026. Well, one of those statements may have a drop of truth to it after the Eagles snapped one streak and preserved another in a 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on an overcast Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak, their longest since 2012, during Andy Reid’s last season. The Eagles also continued their streak at home against Pittsburgh, winning for the 12th-straight time over the Steelers, who have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, (20–14 at Franklin Field), 61 years and two stadiums ago. Maybe the addition of former Eagles’ coach T.J. Paganatti as a consultant had something to do with the Eagles’ offensive line looking the best it has this season. The defense was strong, holding the Steelers to 73 yards rushing, 43 yards below their season average of 116 yards a game, and sacking 42-year-old relic Aaron Rodgers five times for minus-45 yards. Joe Milton was competent, moving the Eagles, especially in clutch situations, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards. Saquon Barkley made a brief appearance as Saquon Barkley rushing for a game-high 75 yards, the bulk of which came on a first quarter 38-yard touchdown run, while Jeremiah Trotter Jr. led the defense with a game-high 13 tackles, Marcus Epps had his best game this season with a season-high 8 tackles, and a bunch of guys who had received very little playing time making significant contributions like Byron Young’s two sacks, Jon Jones’ three defended passes, and Gabe Hall coming off the practice squad for a sack. The Eagles are 3-7. But are they suddenly cured of the slopfest they perpetrated over the first nine games—absolutely not. More proof is demanded. If the Eagles can somehow beat Dallas, in Dallas, on Thanksgiving, with the lowly tanking Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts following them, this nightmare of a season could have life, with the Eagles sitting at 6-7 in an NFC East Division up for grabs. Did Sunday’s victory resuscitate the Eagles or briefly camouflage a bad football team for one week and in the long run hurt its draft status? The answer may be four days from now in Dallas. top.title: Chivas honoured the story of Antonio, a courageous Mexican
top.description: Chivas honoured the story of Antonio, a courageous Mexican A passion for sports, perseverance, and the desire to overcome any obstacle are some of the qualities that set Antonio Vázquez apart. The 17-year-old has turned every challenge into an opportunity to prove his abilities and achieve his goals. In recognition of his effort, hard work, and dedication, Club Deportivo Guadalajara invited him to enjoy an unforgettable experience at Estadio AKRON this Sunday, where he got to share his passion for the red and white up close. Originally from Mérida, Yucatán, Antonio was born with limb agenesis, a condition in which both his feet and his left hand are absent. When he was born, his parents were told he might never be able to walk. However, through tremendous effort, his family's support, and especially his grandmother's unconditional encouragement, he learned to do so and discovered one of his greatest passions in sports. He has played recreational soccer in local tournaments since he was 9, and for the past three years, he has represented Yucatán as a para-athlete in the 100 meters and shot put in the T42/F42 classifications. His dedication has already earned him gold medals in all his events at the state level, as well as standout performances at the CONADE National Paralympics. He has won four medals at this competition: a bronze in Oaxaca in 2024, a gold in the 100 meters in Aguascalientes in 2025, and two silvers—one in shot put in Aguascalientes in 2025 and another in the 100 meters at the 2026 edition held in Guadalajara, Jalisco. A red-and-white heart since 2017 Beyond his passion for sports, Antonio has a deep love for Guadalajara. His journey as a Chivas fan began during the Clausura 2017 Final, when he watched the Sacred Flock win the Liga MX title. From that moment on, he became a loyal supporter of the team, finding in the red and white a passion he shares with his girlfriend. His favorite players include Roberto Alvarado and Hugo Camberos , whom he particularly admires. Antonio has closely followed the young red-and-white player's career since his early days with Tapatío, and even remembers that the first match he saw him play was against Venados de Yucatán. From that game on, he recognized his talent and believed he would make it to the First Team. An unforgettable experience with the Red-and-White Nation! As part of the Mexicanos con Valor initiative, Club Deportivo Guadalajara prepared a very special experience for Antonio, who traveled from Mérida, Yucatán, to the Pearl of Jalisco thanks to the support of Volaris, the team's official sponsor. top.title: No. 10 Iowa State falls at No. 4 Iowa
top.description: Iowa State’s Coby Merril wrestles Iowa’s Ben Kueter in a 285-pound match Nov. 22, 2026 during Cy-Hawk wrestling dual at Carver-Hawkeye Arena in Iowa City, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co IOWA CITY — The Cyclones brought a halftime lead and a wave of momentum into Carver-Hawkeye Arena on Sunday. But when the No. 4 Hawkeyes needed a spark out of the break, their upper-middleweights delivered a decisive response. Behind a dramatic late takedown from Carter Schubert and back-to-back major decisions by Gabe Arnold and Angelo Ferrari, No. 4 Iowa stormed past No. 10 Iowa State 21-12 to reclaim the Dan Gable Traveling Trophy in the annual Iowa Corn Cy-Hawk Dual. The Hawkeyes jumped out to an early 7-0 dual advantage behind strong lower-weight performances. At 125 pounds, 16th-ranked Leo DeLuca opened the afternoon with a dominant 9-0 major decision over No. 29 Rin Sakamoto. Unranked Kale Peterson followed at 133 pounds, pulling off a 2-0 decision over No. 18 Garrett Grice using a second-period escape and a full third-period rideout. The 10th-ranked Cyclones answered with three straight victories from 141 to 157 pounds to take control before intermission. Fourth-ranked Evan Frost got Iowa State on the board at 141 with a 1-0 victory over No. 7 Nasir Bailey, controlling mat position after a second-period escape. His brother Jacob, followed at 149 with a 7-2 win over No. 6 Ryder Block, scoring two takedowns to avenge a loss from the 2022 high school state finals. No. 9 Paniro Johnson then scored a first-period takedown at 157 pounds to edge No. 18 Jordan Williams 4-3, giving Iowa State a 9-7 lead at the break. The dual swung back in Iowa’s favor immediately following intermission at 165 pounds. Locked in a tight battle with No. 17 Connor Euton, No. 9 ranked Carter Schubert executed a clutch takedown with less than 10 seconds remaining on the clock to snatch a 9-8 decision and put the Hawkeyes ahead 10-9. That late heroics opened the floodgates for Iowa’s middle lineup. At 174 pounds, fifth-ranked Gabe Arnold pushed a relentless pace against Tate Naaktgeboren to rack up a 17-6 major decision. Third-ranked freshman Angelo Ferrari kept the pressure on at 184 pounds, controlling Aiden Riggins in a 17-3 major decision that extended Iowa’s lead to 18-9 and put the dual out of reach. Iowa State chipped away at 197 pounds when No. 21 Brayden Thompson accumulated more than a minute of riding time to earn a 3-2 decision over No. 26 Harvey Ludington. However, top-ranked heavyweight Ben Kueter closed the door for the Hawkeyes, breaking a 1-1 tie in sudden-victory overtime with a sweep and takedown to cap a 4-1 decision over No. 12 Coby Merrill. With the victory, Iowa improves to 2-0 on the season, while Iowa State falls to 4-1. The Cyclones return to action Dec. 12–13 at the National Duals Invitational in Tulsa, Oklahoma. top.title: Billie Jean King Cup: Coco Gauff plays doubles, USA sweeps Hungary
top.description: DELRAY BEACH — Brandishing the American flag, Coco Gauff led her USA teammates around the court at Delray Beach Tennis Center. Then, still holding the flag, she danced with it to the rap music. After a late Saturday night that saw a 5 1/2-hour delay in her singles match, Gauff was back playing the key doubles match at 1:30 p.m. Sunday in a late switch by captain Lindsay Davenport . Though Coco rarely plays doubles anymore, she paired with lefty bomber Taylor Townsend , one of the world’s best doubles players and someone the 22-year-old Coco looked up to when she was a young teenager. More BJK Cup: Billie Jean King Cup plagued by thunderstorms, tornado watch It was a wonderful way to end it – two Black players with Palm Beach County roots, one the star of the singles tour, the other the star of the doubles tour. Coco and Townsend shook off a rocky start to repel Hungary’s Anna Bondar and Dalma Galfi 6-4, 6-3 to give USA the clinching third point in the best-of-five Billie Jean Cup qualifier . “I’m glad we closed it out because I didn’t want to play another singles match,’’ Gauff said. “There was always the scenario we’d be up 2-0 and maybe play (doubles) and try to finish it. We were prepared to play with each other. Taylor and Lindsay were confident in my ability to play doubles and then play singles after (if necessary).’’ It wasn’t necessary, but things looked dicey early. In the first set, Coco-Townsend fell behind 3-1 before rallying to win the next 3 games for a 4-3 lead. Still, at 4-4, Coco faced a break point that could’ve put USA behind 5-4. But the pair rallied for a 5-4 lead and closed it out. The second set also was tight before a late surge that gave Townsend-Coco the win and the insurmountable 3-0 USA lead. “I was following her lead for the most part,’’ Coco said. “She is going to go down as one of the greats of the sport (in doubles). Don’t compare me to her. She’s so much better than me. I wasn’t nervous but I hadn’t played doubles in a long time. I was confident but I didn’t play well most of the match.’’ Townsend is coming off winning the season-ending doubles title last week at Indian Wells and also won the Miami Open, French Open and U.S. Open doubles titles. The 30-year-old Townsend bashed about 10 overhead smash winners into the crowd Sunday. “It’s her mentality and positivity to be able to uplift your partner when not playing well,’’ Gauff said of Townsend. “She serves well and has the best hands on tour in my opinion.’’ Coco has very fast hands at the net, too, and came up with superlative volleys. But she also made errors as doubles positioning is different than singles. The two didn’t practice together during the week. Townsend was slated to play with doubles specialist Desirae Krawczyk. “Our first four games was our practice,’’ Townsend quipped. top.title: Skubal agrees to nine-year $450 mln MLB deal with Mets: reports
top.description: Picher Tarik Skubal has reportedly agreed to a nine-year MLB deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets (Patrick McDermott) Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday. The 30-year-old American left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy. The $50 million (45.5 million euros) average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the $43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. Skubal's deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of $325 million set when the Dodgers signed Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024. Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025. He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in earned-run average at 2.39 plus topping MLB in strikeouts with 228. Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL's lowest earned-run average in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195 1/3 innings to repeat. In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded $32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was cut short in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow. He returned in July and after joining the Dodgers, Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by eventual champion Milwaukee. Skubal, considered the top free agent player available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the December 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching. If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month. Owners demand a salary cap system while the union has been against such a format for decades. js/rcw

top.title: DJ Moore Returns After Knee Scare To Score For Bills
top.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images DJ Moore caught a four-yard pass from Josh Allen to score Buffalo’s first touchdown of the game before leaving the field late in the second quarter, according to RotoBaller NFL . Trainers helped the wide receiver to the sideline after he went down on an Allen interception, but he did not stay out long. Following treatment at the medical tent, Moore proceeded to the locker room under his own power, RotoBaller reported. The injury scare happened during a critical moment when the Bills were trying to build momentum against the Miami Dolphins. Moore had already made five catches for 41 yards before the play that sent him to the ground. He was initially listed as questionable to return, which made every fan on the edge of their seat. But the team’s medical staff cleared him to go back into the game. A Quick Return to Action Moore did not waste any time getting back on the field once he was cleared by the trainers. He reentered the game and immediately made an impact with an 18-yard reception. This play showed that his knee was stable enough to handle the physical demands of the NFL. The fact that he could run and catch without limping is a huge relief for the Bills offense. Players often hesitate after a hard hit, especially one that looks as bad as Moore’s did on the replay. His ability to snap back into the game speaks to his toughness and the quality of the medical care he received. RotoBaller reported that he added this 18-yard catch after reentering, proving he was ready to contribute right away. The Bills needed Moore healthy to keep their passing game moving against a strong Miami defense. Losing their top receiver for the rest of the game would have forced Josh Allen to look elsewhere for targets. Instead, Allen found Moore again for the score and the long gain. This shows the trust between the quarterback and his favorite target is still strong. Moore’s five catches for 41 yards before the injury set the tone for the first half. His return ensures the Bills have their primary weapon for the second half of the matchup. The team can now plan their plays around his route running without worrying about his availability. It was a rough moment, but the outcome was positive for the home team. The final stats for Moore include the touchdown and the long catch after his return. His ability to play through the scare keeps the Buffalo attack dangerous for the rest of the season. top.title: Cale Jacobsen Saves the Day with Game Winner for Nebraska in 76-74 Win Over Butler
top.description: Nebraska's Cale Jacobsen (31) reacts afer the final shot during a second-round game in the NCAA men's basketball tournament between Nebraska Cornhuskers and Vanderbilt Commodores at Paycom Center in Oklahoma City, Saturday March 21, 2026. | SARAH PHIPPS/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images It was back and forth the entire game. Butler dragged Nebraska into a game it was not ready for but the Huskers were able to keep it close all the way to the end. With one minute left in the game, Jacob Lanier fed Damon Wilkinson in the post who finished around the rim to tie the game at 74. Butler called a timeout. Then they got their best three point shooter, Asim Djulovic, enough space to get a shot off but he missed. Pryce Sandfort got the rebound and Fred Hoiberg called a timeout with 23 seconds left in the game. Who does Hoiberg go to in this moment? The Ashland-Greenwood product, Cale Jacobsen. top.title: Leaders Barcelona make impressive Villarreal comeback, Atletico triumph
top.description: Villarreal defender Pau Navarro's own goal handed Barcelona the three points in their La Liga win at Camp Nou (Josep LAGO) Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Later Sunday, Atletico Madrid won 3-0 away at Getafe to stay on the trail of Spain's top two after a defeat in their previous outing by Barca. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty. However, the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro's own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. "We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I'll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn't happen again," Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed his team's comeback, something they have made a habit of during his reign. "We made two mistakes and they scored two times... but the reaction that we had was unbelievable," Flick told reporters. The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance. Two minutes later, Villarreal doubled their advantage when Oluwaseyi smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Flick's side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area, but the teenage winger dragged his penalty against the post and wide. - Quickfire treble - Barcelona quickly dragged themselves back into the match after the interval. Martin found the net in the 57th minute with a header from Pedri's cross. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Peter Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Lopez, who had been substituted off, was sent off for dissent as Barca protested on the sidelines. Flick said although he was happy with refereeing in Spain generally, he disliked Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez. "We saw which referee was there and we expect it," said Flick. "I'm really happy with the referees but with this referee -- not." Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, 10th, left frustrated

nigeria.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. nigeria.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. nigeria.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
nigeria.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

nigeria.title: Man United suffer 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first match as coach
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. nigeria.title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku
nigeria.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu. Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal. “Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said. Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters. “Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said. He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate. “If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said. The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress. He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates. “Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said. On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households. He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country. “Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards. He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters. “I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said. The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. I’m so thankful now for getting offers to play at the next level.” Eastern Michigan proved to be that right opportunity, with his official visit to Ypsilanti sealing the deal for Truss. “I would say the coaches, their hospitality, and their interest in me made me want to be there. And I liked the facilities, the meeting rooms and all that,” Truss said. With that, Truss now prepares for the next step of his journey, which is enrolling mid-year at Eastern Michigan. “Getting this opportunity, coming from where I’m from and being through what I’ve been through, I just am very thankful,” Truss said. sports.title: ‘Worse outcome’ – Mike Pettine’s defense was worse than Christian Parker’s, says former Dallas Cowboys star
sports.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Tennessee Titans to move to 5-6… But what about their defense? Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys’ offense stole the show against the Titans, winning 51-30. Ahead of the game, all the talk was about the team’s defense, after they promoted Mike Pettine to call plays in place of defensive coordinator Christian Parker. The switch was a response to the 46-40 loss to the 49ers, in which the Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards. Speaking after the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was pleased with the way the defense played. He told his press conference: “Overall, I was very proud of the defensive unit, coaches, and everybody.” But his response did not please former Cowboys wide receiver Isaiah Stanback, who told the Cowboys’ postgame show that he felt the defense actually went backwards. He pointed to the fact the team gave up 30 points against a Titans team that is now 1-9 in the standings. Isaiah Stanback: Cowboys went backwards “I don’t wholly agree with him,” Stanback said, in response to Schottenheimer being proud of the Cowboys’ defense. He explained: “Last [week], he faced one of the more prominent offenses in the [offensive] play caller, and some of the most dangerous weapons in the NFL. He faced one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL, Brock Purdy. “Christian McCaffrey, one of the best running backs you have played in the game, as far as catching the ball, running the ball. “You got five sacks against [a] San Francisco 49ers outfit. You got five sacks against the Tennessee outfit that has Cam Ward, has Tony Pollard, Chimere Dike, that’s a big difference, right? “You gave up 46 last week. You gave up 30 to a Tennessee Titans team, that came in averaging 18 points per game. “So you can feel as if you performed better, but in reality, if I’m looking at it in totality, yes, you gave up more yards. Yes, you gave up bigger plays. All that stuff last week, but it was against a substantially better outfit. “So, to me, as I look at this, I think giving up 30 to this outfit is actually a worse outcome than even what you faced last [week], in my opinion.” The Cowboys’ defense will be tested next against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, who secured a surprise 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. sports.title: It’s a Deal! Skubal to the Mets!
sports.description: Sep 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images It’s Official! Tarik Skubal is a New York Met . The New York Mets have agreed to terms with two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal on a nine-year, $450 million contract , according to multiple reports on Sunday. The deal, first reported by the New York Post’s Jon Heyman and confirmed in its terms by ESPN’s Jeff Passan, sets a new standard as the richest contract ever given to a pitcher in MLB history. The agreement includes a $45 million signing bonus, full no-trade protection, and no opt-out clauses. Roughly $30 million is deferred. The average annual value comes to $50 million, also a record for a pitcher and well clear of the previous high-water marks set by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. It eclipses Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s 12-year, $325 million pact with the Dodgers by $125 million in total value. Skubal, who turned 30 last week, becomes the centerpiece of a Mets rotation that already features promising right-hander Nolan McLean. He joins a lineup built around Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette. For owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns, the signing is the clearest statement yet that the club intends to rebound from a disappointing 2026 season and contend immediately in 2027. The left-hander’s path to free agency was eventful. After winning consecutive Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025 with the Detroit Tigers, he underwent a procedure in May 2026 to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. He returned in roughly six weeks and was later traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers ahead of the deadline. Across both clubs in 2026, he went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings. Because he changed teams midseason, the Dodgers could not make him a qualifying offer, so the Mets incur no draft-pick penalty for the signing. Skubal’s free-agent process moved quickly. He held in-person meetings last week in California with the Mets, Dodgers, Blue Jays, and Padres. New York was widely viewed as the favorite after an early offer in the neighborhood of nine years and nearly $400 million. Agent Scott Boras had indicated a strong likelihood the left-hander would decide before the collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1. Over the past three seasons, Skubal has posted a 2.42 ERA, ranking among the game’s elite in strikeouts, innings, and Wins Above Replacement. He has also shown postseason pedigree, with a career 2.13 ERA in eight playoff starts. The Mets are betting that version of Skubal remains the one who takes the mound in Queens for the rest of the decade.

Joe Milton was competent, moving the Eagles, especially in clutch situations, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards. sports.description: Iowa State’s Coby Merril wrestles Iowa’s Ben Kueter in a 285-pound match Nov. 22, 2026 during Cy-Hawk wrestling dual at Carver-Hawkeye Arena in Iowa City, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co IOWA CITY — The Cyclones brought a halftime lead and a wave of momentum into Carver-Hawkeye Arena on Sunday. But when the No. 4 Hawkeyes needed a spark out of the break, their upper-middleweights delivered a decisive response. Behind a dramatic late takedown from Carter Schubert and back-to-back major decisions by Gabe Arnold and Angelo Ferrari, No. 4 Iowa stormed past No. 10 Iowa State 21-12 to reclaim the Dan Gable Traveling Trophy in the annual Iowa Corn Cy-Hawk Dual. The Hawkeyes jumped out to an early 7-0 dual advantage behind strong lower-weight performances. At 125 pounds, 16th-ranked Leo DeLuca opened the afternoon with a dominant 9-0 major decision over No. 29 Rin Sakamoto. Unranked Kale Peterson followed at 133 pounds, pulling off a 2-0 decision over No. 18 Garrett Grice using a second-period escape and a full third-period rideout. The 10th-ranked Cyclones answered with three straight victories from 141 to 157 pounds to take control before intermission. Fourth-ranked Evan Frost got Iowa State on the board at 141 with a 1-0 victory over No. 7 Nasir Bailey, controlling mat position after a second-period escape. His brother Jacob, followed at 149 with a 7-2 win over No. 6 Ryder Block, scoring two takedowns to avenge a loss from the 2022 high school state finals. No. 9 Paniro Johnson then scored a first-period takedown at 157 pounds to edge No. 18 Jordan Williams 4-3, giving Iowa State a 9-7 lead at the break. The dual swung back in Iowa’s favor immediately following intermission at 165 pounds. Third-ranked freshman Angelo Ferrari kept the pressure on at 184 pounds, controlling Aiden Riggins in a 17-3 major decision that extended Iowa’s lead to 18-9 and put the dual out of reach. Then, still holding the flag, she danced with it to the rap music. sports.title: Skubal agrees to nine-year $450 mln MLB deal with Mets: reports
sports.description: Picher Tarik Skubal has reportedly agreed to a nine-year MLB deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets (Patrick McDermott) Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday. The 30-year-old American left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy. The $50 million (45.5 million euros) average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the $43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. Skubal's deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of $325 million set when the Dodgers signed Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024. Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025. He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in earned-run average at 2.39 plus topping MLB in strikeouts with 228. Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL's lowest earned-run average in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195 1/3 innings to repeat. In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded $32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was cut short in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow. He returned in July and after joining the Dodgers, Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by eventual champion Milwaukee. Skubal, considered the top free agent player available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the December 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching. If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month. sports.title: Leaders Barcelona make impressive Villarreal comeback, Atletico triumph
sports.description: Villarreal defender Pau Navarro's own goal handed Barcelona the three points in their La Liga win at Camp Nou (Josep LAGO) Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Later Sunday, Atletico Madrid won 3-0 away at Getafe to stay on the trail of Spain's top two after a defeat in their previous outing by Barca. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty. However, the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro's own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. "We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I'll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn't happen again," Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed his team's comeback, something they have made a habit of during his reign. "We made two mistakes and they scored two times... but the reaction that we had was unbelievable," Flick told reporters. The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance. Two minutes later, Villarreal doubled their advantage when Oluwaseyi smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Flick's side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area, but the teenage winger dragged his penalty against the post and wide. - Quickfire treble - Barcelona quickly dragged themselves back into the match after the interval. Martin found the net in the 57th minute with a header from Pedri's cross. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Peter Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Lopez, who had been substituted off, was sent off for dissent as Barca protested on the sidelines. Flick said although he was happy with refereeing in Spain generally, he disliked Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez. "We saw which referee was there and we expect it," said Flick. "I'm really happy with the referees but with this referee -- not." Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, 10th, left frustrated

technology.title: As cars go digital, US consumers pay an extra $12 billion a year for repairs
technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is. DIY repairers should be able to get everything they need to fix their own cars. science.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong?
